name: What is the difference between repairing and replacing exterior wood elements?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between repairing and replacing exterior wood elements?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing exterior wood elements involves addressing localized damage, such as patching small areas of rot or replacing a few damaged boards. This is cost-effective if the damage is minimal and confined. Replacement, on the other hand, entails removing and installing entirely new sections or structures, like a whole fence line or an entire wall of siding. Replacement is necessary when damage is extensive, widespread, or compromises the structural integrity, making repair impractical or short-lived.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repairing fixes small, localized damage, while replacing involves installing new sections when damage is extensive or structural.
